title: ARPANET’s first message was just “lo”, then the computer crashed
body: On 29 October 1969, UCLA student programmer Charley Kline tried to log in to a computer at the Stanford Research Institute over ARPANET, the network that grew into the internet. He got as far as “L” and “O” before the SRI system crashed. About an hour later the full login worked. By the end of 1969, ARPANET linked just four sites.

steps.label: UCLA student Charley Kline types L
He types O: ‘lo’ has crossed the network
About an hour later, the full login works

slides.question: How many sites did ARPANET, the network that grew into the internet, connect by the end of 1969?
slides.explanation: By the end of 1969 ARPANET linked just four sites. The first login attempt, from UCLA to the Stanford Research Institute, crashed after two letters.

slides.heading: Which was not one of the first four ARPANET sites?
slides.explanation: The first four nodes, all in the western US, were UCLA, SRI, UC Santa Barbara and the University of Utah. BBN’s node near Boston joined in March 1970.
